newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares seen drifting ahead of results.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares seen drifting ahead of results.

text.p: Belgian shares recovered from a weak start on Monday to stand little changed in directionless trade at midday.
Investor focus was fixed later on the week and the first heavy crop of corporate results, dealers said.
"It's pretty quiet," one trader said. "All the results... might give the market some direction."
Bel-20 earnings statements are due this week from Generale Bank (Tuesday), CBR (Wednesday) and Kredietbank and Union Miniere (Thursday).

Outside the Bel-20, results include those from, on Wednesday, industrial foams group Recticel and, on Thursday, temporary employment group Creyf's Interim, commodities group Sipef and natural gas distributor Distrigas.

Volume was thin in early business on Monday. But bank shares were animated by merger talk, with BBL rising 60 francs to 8,150 francs and Generale Bank up 150 francs at 13,250 francs after Generale Bank shareholder SGB reiterated it would favour a merger of the two.
